sections.title: 5.4. Ablation on Other Thinking Control Methods

abstract_sentences.text: Recent progress in multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) has significantly improved reasoning LLMs’ performances on complex interactive tasks.
Despite advances in stabilization techniques such as fine-grained credit assignment and trajectory filtering, instability remains pervasive and often leads to training collapse.

We argue that this instability stems from inefficient exploration in multi-turn settings, where policies continue to generate low-information actions that neither reduce uncertainty nor advance task progress.

evidence.anchor: neither reduce uncertainty nor advance task progress

abstract_sentences.text: To address this issue, we propose Token- and Turn-level Policy Optimization (T2PO), an uncertainty-aware framework that explicitly controls exploration at fine-grained levels.

evidence.anchor: explicitly controls exploration at fine-grained levels

abstract_sentences.text: At the token level, T2PO monitors uncertainty dynamics and triggers a thinking intervention once the marginal uncertainty change falls below a threshold.

evidence.anchor: marginal uncertainty change falls below a threshold

abstract_sentences.text: At the turn level, T2PO identifies interactions with negligible exploration progress and dynamically resamples such turns to avoid wasted rollouts.

We evaluate T2PO in diverse environments, including WebShop, ALFWorld, and Search QA, demonstrating substantial gains in training stability and performance improvements with better exploration efficiency.

claim_closure.claim: Inefficient exploration/hesitation is the root cause of training collapse.
claim_closure.method_response: M identifies token/turn uncertainty patterns; TTI and TDS intervene on them.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 1/5, ablations, and qualitative cases show correlated failure/efficiency patterns, but no mediator or counterfactual test isolates the causal path.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 restates suppression of low-information action and collapse mitigation.

evidence.anchor: without collapse on three different env seeds

claim_closure.claim: Entropy and confidence are complementary and M is a better stability signal.
claim_closure.method_response: Equations (1)-(3) normalize and fuse H/C; Figure 3 supplies contour intuition.
claim_closure.evidence_response: α Table 7 and main results provide indirect support; no calibration metric, formal geometry theorem, or non-WebShop sweep is provided.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 only recalls intrinsic-signal regulation, not the contour claim.

claim_closure.claim: TTI reduces redundant token reasoning while preserving useful reasoning.
claim_closure.method_response: Windowed Δ trigger, forced terminator, deterministic queue, one-time activation, and Lmax.
claim_closure.evidence_response: w/o TTI, Figure 5/6, and over-thinking case support performance/format direction; no token-level utility-preservation or trigger-frequency mediation test.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 says low-information action is suppressed without additional reward shaping.

evidence.anchor: truncation would likely occur on task-specific tokens

claim_closure.claim: TDS suppresses repeated cross-turn reasoning and maintains trajectory diversity.
claim_closure.method_response: Φ/Γ signal and same-state regeneration until η or Bmax.
claim_closure.evidence_response: w/o TDS, Figure 5/7, and repeated-failure case support direction; no direct diversity or convergence statistic.

evidence.anchor: semantically similar but failed reasoning traces

claim_closure.claim: T2PO generalizes across WebShop, ALFWorld, and Search QA.
claim_closure.method_response: Unified rollout and policy-update pipeline with task-specific Table 5 settings.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Tables 1-2 cover the three settings, but model family and tasks are narrow; Search QA prose contains a MuSiQue mismatch.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 makes a broad consistency claim without narrowing to Qwen3/these benchmarks.

evidence.anchor: three public available challenging interactive benchmarks

claim_closure.claim: T2PO improves stability without additional reward shaping or extra model parameters.
claim_closure.method_response: Uses intrinsic M control but also RFT, format penalty, memory window, and hierarchical advantage.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 1/3, Figure 5, and Table 6 support composite-pipeline stability; no factorial design separates TTI/TDS from RFT/format penalty.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 repeats “without relying on additional reward shaping.”

evidence.anchor: rather than introducing additional reward shaping

claim_closure.claim: The control is plug-and-play across policy optimizers.
claim_closure.method_response: TTI/TDS are presented around the rollout/control boundary, separate from policy loss.
claim_closure.evidence_response: One WebShop GSPO replacement raises Success 85.18→91.79; evidence is direct but limited to one optimizer/task.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: No separate conclusion sentence; Appendix D.1 states the integration claim.

claim_closure.claim: T2PO improves token and turn efficiency.
claim_closure.method_response: TTI truncates after stable token signal; TDS regenerates low-difference turns.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figures 5-7 and stated 20%/25%/16% reductions provide directional/percentage evidence, but definitions and denominators are absent.

limitations.name: off_policy_staleness
limitations.description: Pipelined rollout/update introduces stale snapshots; longer horizons and larger rollout batches amplify staleness, importance-weight variance, and instability. Table 6 covers only three WebShop settings.

lexical_analysis.interpretation: Training/exploration/reasoning and token/turn terms drive the real argument; case/template and figure/table terms inflate extracted counts. Strong result verbs outnumber explicit uncertainty markers, while the paper uses roughly/substantially/consistently to soften magnitudes.

final_judgment.single_storyline: Multi-turn RL collapse is attributed to hesitation: low-information token continuation and repeated low-information turns. T2PO turns uncertainty dynamics into token-level TTI and turn-level TDS, then combines them with hierarchical credit assignment.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: Problem and collapse visualization; M/TTI/TDS definitions; forced structured output; policy objective; three task families; main result/ablation tables; Figure 5 efficiency direction; conclusion.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Reward and EM definitions, hyperparameters, RFT/parser/staleness, alternative controls, GSPO, length/α/ALFWorld analyses, reward decomposition, pseudocode, and case studies. This preserves conceptual flow but makes statistics, thresholds, and failure boundaries appendix-dependent.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 2 process overview plus Figure 3 signal geometry and Figure 4 trigger intuition create an object→mechanism→action progression; Tables 3-4 align component deletion and alternative-control comparisons on one WebShop scale.
final_judgment.largest_gap: The MuSiQue prose claim conflicts with Table 2; §5.5 mislabels Figure 5 as Figure 7; promised ε/η/N sweeps are absent; ±, denominators, seeds, and episode counts are undefined. No formal stability/utility guarantee or causal separation from RFT/format penalty is supplied.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a multi-scale control contribution, give each scale one observable signal, one executable trigger, one deletion experiment, and one efficiency estimand with denominator and uncertainty definition in the main decision path.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule fits agentic RL with hierarchical states, observable process signals, and measurable rollout cost. When process signals or same-state regeneration are unavailable, Φ/Γ semantics and causal identification require separate validation.

evidence_coverage.coverage_note: All substantive entries in this reading carry at least one physical PDF page, section, and short anchor; absent items use not_present or unavailable where applicable.

reading_protocol.module_metric_contract: Exactly one entry for each of the 12 required semantic modules.

word_count_basis.module_estimate_note: Section estimates are PDF extraction counts allocated by physical section; table/figure/equation text can cause small overcounts. Appendix and non-main front/back matter are not included in the main_word_share denominator.
word_count_basis.main_ranges: p.1-p.8 main prose/table/formula extraction = 5,241 raw word tokens; module shares use 5,171 allocated section words after visual/front-matter allocation.
